title: Manufacturer's licence to sell alcohol in Ontario
plain_language_summary: Any producer selling alcohol into Ontario, whether shipping directly to consumers or through retail, needs a manufacturer's licence from the AGCO before any sales can occur.
raw_requirement_text: Under the Liquor Licence and Control Act, a manufacturer must hold a valid licence issued by the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario prior to manufacturing, selling, or distributing liquor in Ontario.
authority: Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO)

title: Ontario alcohol labeling and container standards
plain_language_summary: Bottles sold in Ontario need specific label disclosures (alcohol content, standard drink info, warnings) that may differ from your home province's requirements.
raw_requirement_text: Products sold within Ontario must meet AGCO-specified labeling standards distinct from federal Food and Drugs Act minimums.
authority: Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO)

title: Federal meat inspection for interprovincial sale
plain_language_summary: To legally sell meat products across a provincial border into or out of Ontario, your facility must be federally (CFIA) inspected, not just provincially licensed.
raw_requirement_text: Meat products moved in interprovincial trade require inspection under the Safe Food for Canadians Regulations administered by the Canadian Food Inspection Agency.

title: Commercial Vehicle Operator's Registration (CVOR)
plain_language_summary: Businesses operating commercial trucks in Ontario need a CVOR certificate, and safety ratings are tracked provincially.
raw_requirement_text: Operators of commercial motor vehicles registered in Ontario or operating within Ontario must hold a valid CVOR certificate under the Highway Traffic Act.

title: Provincial professional licensing recognition
plain_language_summary: Regulated professions (e.g. engineering, accounting, trades) generally require registration with the relevant Ontario regulatory body, though Bill C-5's labour mobility provisions are expanding federal recognition of out-of-province credentials.
raw_requirement_text: Individuals practising a regulated profession in Ontario must be registered with the applicable Ontario regulatory college or association, subject to labour mobility exceptions under the Free Trade and Labour Mobility in Canada Act.
authority: Relevant Ontario regulatory college (varies by profession)
